values.event_label: Adds a new '### Networking' subsection to the Specification defining a replacement for the EIP-4844 blob-transaction pool wrapper used in PooledTransactions responses: rlp([tx_payload_body, wrapper_version, blobs, commitments, cell_proofs]), with wrapper_version = 1, cell_proofs carrying CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB proofs per blob (extension cells included, blobs sent unextended), the indexing rule cell_proofs[i * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB + j], and four MUST validation conditions the receiving node applies (equal counts, exact cell-proof count, versioned-hash match, commitment/blob/cell-proof consistency with batch verification). Also repoints the detailed-specification link from consensus-specs specs/_features/eip7594/das-core.md (commit b4188829) to the specs/fulu/ tree (commit 9d377fd5).
values.rationale: Introduces a new normative wire data structure and validation rules for blob transactions; the first execution-layer-observable requirement in the document.

values.eip_label: EIP-7594 · PeerDAS - Peer Data Availability Sampling
values.event_label: Large content expansion ahead of Last Call. Frontmatter: category Networking -> Core and author Alex Stokes (@ralexstokes) added. Replaces the 'TBD' Rationale with five subsections (why DAS scales the DA layer and the 1/8 sampling fraction, what peer sampling provides, why the parameters were chosen, why validators have a custody requirement beyond full nodes, column vs row sampling). Adds a Backwards Compatibility statement ('fully backwards compatible with EIP-4844'), replaces the empty Reference Implementation heading with a Test Cases pointer to the consensus and execution spec tests, and replaces 'Needs discussion' in Security Considerations with a data-withholding analysis including the explicit upper bound P(tricking n*epsilon nodes) <= C(n, n*eps) * C(m, m/2 - 1) * 2^(-k*n*eps) and a table of bounds for 10,000 nodes. Wording touch-ups in the abstract and specification (beacon nodes -> nodes, custody phrasing, wrapper_version emphasis, compute_cells / verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch named).
values.rationale: Adds the document's security argument and its formal withholding bound, and reclassifies the EIP from Networking to Core. Classified security_assumption because the security analysis is the largest normative-relevant addition; no MUST requirement changed. Medium confidence on the change_type because the commit is a mixed rationale/security/metadata update.

values.event_label: Renames the consensus-layer configuration field and its keys: `BPO_FORK` -> `BLOB_SCHEDULE`, `epoch` -> `EPOCH`, `max_blobs` -> `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK`, and updates the matching requirement to read 'The `max` field in `blobSchedule` MUST equal the `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK` value in the consensus layer configuration'.
values.rationale: Renames the consensus-layer configuration field and keys that clients must implement, and restates a MUST requirement in the new terms.
values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit 954213305a: Update EIP-7892: Consensus Config Format

values.event_label: Largest single expansion of the EIP. Adds author Raul Kripalani (@raulk). Restructures the Specification into Definition / Blob schedule configuration / Execution layer configuration / Consensus layer configuration subsections. Execution layer: each blobSchedule fork is now linked to activation via a top-level `<fork_name>Time` Unix-timestamp field, BPO forks SHOULD be named `bpo<index>` starting at 1, activation timestamps are required only for post-Prague forks, and the illustrative JSON switches from raw-timestamp keys to named osaka/bpo1/bpo2 entries plus cancunTime/pragueTime/osakaTime/bpo1Time/bpo2Time. Adds the rule that a regular hardfork changing these parameters MUST do so by adding a blob schedule entry. Consensus layer: `BLOB_SCHEDULE` is defined as the sequence of blob-parameter changes after ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH, one entry per changing fork. Adds a modified `compute_fork_digest` taking `current_epoch` and `blob_schedule` and XOR-bitmasking `max_blobs_per_block` into the 4-byte digest (returning the base digest when no schedule entry applies). Adds a P2P Networking section: a new ENR entry `nfd` (SSZ Bytes4 ForkDigest, 'next fork digest') that nodes MUST evaluate alongside ENRForkID::next_* fields, a note that `Status` req/resp is unchanged but must carry the updated fork_digest, and a note that gossip topics rotate automatically at a BPO fork. Drops the earlier requirement 'BPO forks MUST NOT conflict with other fork schedules' and changes 'The timestamp in blobSchedule' to 'The slot number in the EL's blobSchedule'.
values.rationale: Introduces new normative networking behaviour (fork-digest computation, ENR field, peer evaluation), a new activation-timestamp configuration mechanism, and removes one previously stated MUST NOT requirement.
values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit f37240a9ae: Update EIP-7892: harden the spec with p2p details.

values.event_label: Adds a fourth managed parameter `maxBlobsPerTx` (maximum blobs per transaction) to the abstract, the managed-parameter list and the illustrative blobSchedule JSON (osaka 6, bpo1 12, bpo2 12), with the requirement that the field is optional, defaults to `max` when omitted, and is not used by the consensus layer. Adds a 'Transaction Pool considerations' subsection stating that transactions exceeding a post-BPO-fork blob count MUST NOT be propagated and should be considered for eviction. Also changes the illustrative osaka entry from target 9 / max 12 to target 6 / max 9.
values.rationale: Adds a new configurable protocol parameter and a new MUST NOT propagation rule for the transaction pool.
values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit 79adba6a17: Update EIP-7892: Add blob count per tx limit via blobSchedule

values.event_label: Reverses the previous commit's addition: removes `maxBlobsPerTx` from the abstract, the managed-parameter list, the illustrative blobSchedule JSON and the requirements list, and deletes the 'Transaction Pool considerations' subsection. The same commit adds the equivalent requirement (a limit of 6 blobs per transaction that clients MUST enforce) to EIPS/eip-7594.md, so the requirement moves from EIP-7892 to EIP-7594.
values.rationale: Removes a configurable parameter and a MUST NOT propagation rule from this EIP; the requirement is relocated to EIP-7594 by the same commit. Recorded in both EIP records under the shared change_group.
